top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Le Race's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.

Road-specific control matters at Le Race. Practice on sealed roads crossing the Port Hills and Banks: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 62 miles.
98ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
6,070ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Le Race, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
62 miles on sealed roads crossing the Port Hills and Banks burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Le Race. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Le Race. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
6,070ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on sealed roads crossing the Port Hills and Banks can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 6,070ft of climbing on sealed roads crossing the Port Hills and Banks does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 6,070ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for Le Race's 62 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Le Race rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on sealed roads crossing the port hills and banks peninsula volcanic complex to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 62 miles of sealed roads crossing the port hills and banks peninsula volcanic complex in Christchurch to Akaroa, Canterbury, New Zealand.
